airport: Airports show long, straight runways with distinct markings, connected to large terminal buildings, hangars, and parking structures. They differ from industrial areas by having runways and aircraft rather than factories; commercial areas show retail buildings and parking rather than runways; railway stations have train tracks and platforms rather than runways.
beach: Beaches appear as sandy or pebbly shorelines along water bodies, with light colors, wave patterns, and occasional beach umbrellas. They contrast with rivers by being coastal or lakeshore rather than inland waterways; mountains show elevated rocky terrain; ponds are small still water bodies without sandy shores.
bridge: Bridges show elevated roadway or railway structures spanning over water or valleys, with visible pillars, deck, and approach ramps. They differ from viaducts by spanning over water rather than land with multiple supports; ponds are small water bodies without bridges; commercial areas show buildings rather than crossing structures.
commercial: Commercial areas show dense retail and office buildings with large parking lots, wide streets, and visible storefronts or signage. They contrast with parking lots by having buildings alongside vehicle storage; industrial zones show warehouses and smokestacks rather than retail; residential areas show housing units rather than commercial blocks.
desert: Deserts show vast, barren landscapes with sand dunes, rocky outcrops, and sparse dry vegetation, with uniform light tones. They contrast with farmland by lacking crop rows and irrigation; mountains show elevated rocky peaks; airports show runways and terminals rather than dunes.
farmland: Farmland appears as large, open agricultural fields with uniform crop rows, regular field boundaries, and occasional irrigation circles. It differs from desert by having organized crops and vegetation rather than sand; meadow shows natural grassland without field lines; industrial areas show factories and storage rather than crops.
footballfield: Football fields show rectangular grassy areas with clear boundary lines, goal zones, and often surrounding tracks or stands. They contrast with meadow by having sports markings and maintained grass rather than natural vegetation; parks have walking paths and trees rather than field markings; airports show runways and terminals rather than sports fields.
forest: Forests show dense tree canopy with dark green textures, irregular edges, and no visible ground, often covering large areas. They contrast with mountains by having vegetation cover rather than exposed rock; rivers show water channels rather than tree cover; parks have more open spaces and paths rather than dense forest canopy.
industrial: Industrial areas feature large warehouses, factories, smokestacks, and extensive parking lots with regular blocky layouts. They differ from commercial areas by having more warehouses and smokestacks rather than retail storefronts; parking lots show vehicle storage without buildings; airports have runways and terminals rather than industrial structures.
meadow: Meadows show open, grassy areas with smooth, uniform texture, often with scattered trees or shrubs, and no field lines. They contrast with football fields by lacking sports markings and maintained grass; farmland shows organized crop rows rather than natural grassland; parks have paths and recreational areas rather than open meadow.
mountain: Mountains show elevated, rugged terrain with steep slopes, rocky outcrops, and shadow patterns, often with forested lower elevations. They contrast with forests by having exposed rock and elevation changes rather than uniform tree cover; deserts show flat sand dunes rather than rocky peaks; beaches show coastal sandy areas rather than mountainous terrain.
park: Parks show green open spaces with trees, walking paths, ponds, and recreational areas, often irregular in shape. They differ from ponds by being larger areas with vegetation and paths rather than just water; forests have denser canopy with no paths or open areas; commercial areas show buildings and parking rather than parkland.
parking: Parking lots appear as flat, paved areas with rows of vehicles, clear lane markings, and entrance/exit points. They differ from commercial areas by having vehicle storage rather than buildings; ports show water and ships rather than vehicle rows; viaducts show elevated road structures rather than ground-level parking.
pond: Ponds appear as small, circular or irregular water bodies with calm surfaces, often surrounded by vegetation. They contrast with rivers by being still, enclosed water rather than flowing channels; parks are larger green areas with paths and trees rather than just water; bridges are structures crossing water rather than water features themselves.
port: Ports show waterfront areas with docks, piers, ships, cranes, and large storage areas adjacent to water. They differ from parking lots by having ships and water rather than vehicles; bridges are crossing structures rather than waterfront facilities; ponds are small inland water bodies without port infrastructure.
railwaystation: Railway stations show tracks, platforms, passenger buildings, and surrounding parking lots, often with linear rail lines. They contrast with industrial areas by having passenger buildings and platforms rather than factories; viaducts show elevated rail structures rather than ground-level stations; airports have runways rather than train tracks.
residential: Residential areas show housing units with visible roofs, yards, driveways, and street networks, with varied lot sizes. They differ from commercial areas by having housing rather than retail buildings; parks show green open spaces without houses; industrial areas have factories and storage rather than homes.
river: Rivers appear as narrow, sinuous, dark water channels with flowing patterns and riparian vegetation along banks. They contrast with ponds by being elongated flowing water rather than still, enclosed water bodies; beaches show sandy shorelines along water rather than water channels; forests show tree cover without water features.
viaduct: Viaducts show elevated road or rail structures with long continuous sections and multiple supports, often crossing over land. They differ from bridges by spanning over land rather than water; parking lots are ground-level open areas; railway stations are ground-level with tracks rather than elevated structures.
